blocks.text: A.I.R. Gallery invites emerging women and non-binary visual artists based in New York City to apply for its year-long Fellowship Program, which offers six artists mentorship, professional development, curatorial support, a $3,000 stipend, and their first solo exhibition in New York City.
Open Call:

Applications are open for the 2027–2028 A.I.R. Fellowship Program, a 12-month professional development opportunity for emerging and underrepresented women and non-binary visual artists based in New York City.

Running from September 2027 to August 2028, the programme selects six artists annually. It provides each Fellow with professional development workshops, mentorship, studio visits, curatorial support, and a solo exhibition at A.I.R. Gallery in spring or summer 2028. Each Fellow also receives a $3,000 stipend.
Institutional Context:

Established in 1993 by artist Stephanie Bernheim, the A.I.R. Fellowship Program has supported more than 130 artists in realising their first solo exhibition in New York City. The programme helps artists develop sustainable practices while creating opportunities for experimentation, professional exchange, and intergenerational dialogue.

A.I.R. Gallery is a longstanding feminist arts organisation founded in New York in 1972. The Fellowship forms part of its broader commitment to supporting women and non-binary artists and addressing underrepresentation within the contemporary art landscape.
Since 2009, the youngest annual recipient has held the Emma Bee Bernstein Fellowship seat. Since 2024, A.I.R. has also named one participant annually as the Louise H. McCagg Fellow.
Eligibility and Criteria:
Applicants must be women or non-binary visual artists working in any medium and must be aged 18 or older.

Artists must reside in one of New York City’s five boroughs, Manhattan, Queens, Brooklyn, the Bronx or Staten Island, for the full duration of the Fellowship. Applicants do not need to be American citizens, but A.I.R. cannot provide visa sponsorship.

Applicants must not have had a solo exhibition at a permanent venue in New York City during the previous ten years. Exhibitions at temporary or pop-up spaces, art fairs and non-art venues do not make an applicant ineligible.

Artists must not be enrolled in a degree-granting programme or participating in a comparable fellowship, residency or professional development programme during the Fellowship period. Current A.I.R. members, employees, and board members; previous A.I.R. Fellowship recipients; and artists who have previously had a solo exhibition at A.I.R. are not eligible.
Collaborative artist teams may apply, provided they demonstrate an established history of working together and propose a collaborative exhibition.
Evaluation Process:
The selection process is completely anonymous and takes place across three rounds. A three-person external panel of curators, critics, and established artists reviews applications.

Artists are assessed according to the quality of and commitment to their work, as well as their potential to benefit significantly from the Fellowship’s support. A.I.R. members and staff conduct final interviews and selections, with six artists ultimately awarded Fellowships.
The 2027–2028 selection panel comprises Ada Potter, Joey Tang and Mindy Seu. Successful applicants will be notified in April 2027.
Practical Information:
The Fellowship runs from September 2027 to August 2028.
Each selected artist receives:

• A $3,000 stipend • A solo exhibition at A.I.R. Gallery in spring or summer 2028 • Four to five professional development workshops during fall 2027 • An A.I.R. artist mentor for the duration of the programme • A one-on-one studio visit with a selection panellist • Ongoing studio visits and support from A.I.R. staff

Fellows are expected to participate actively in the A.I.R. community and attend programme activities in person. Mandatory requirements include presenting the solo exhibition, holding a group discussion during the exhibition and participating in the programme’s professional development workshops.
Applications and Queries:

Applications close on 10 November 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. A free online information session will take place on 29 October 2026 at 6:30 PM ET, and a recording will be available for applicants unable to attend.

Applications are submitted online through Submittable. Applicants should provide examples of their strongest and most representative work created within the past three years rather than sketches or works in progress.

Importantly, the application process is anonymous. Applicants must ensure their name does not appear anywhere in submitted materials, including filenames, images, statements, CVs or other documents. Applications containing the artist’s name will be disqualified.
